newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong's CKI, Kerry up in infrastructure plays.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong's CKI, Kerry up in infrastructure plays.

text.p: Cheung Kong Infrastructure Holdings Ltd and Kerry Properties advanced sharply in Tuesday morning trading, prompted by renewed interest in China infrastructure plays, brokers said.
"China infrastructure plays have been the focus for the past two to three trading days," said Boby Ho, chief dealer at G.K. Goh Securities.
One local broker said it was a case of catch-up and market reassessment of the two issues.
"Both CKI and Kerry Properties did not do especially well when they were listed, and now some traders and some institutional portfolios see the need to have the stock," a local broker said.

CKI added HK$0.35 to HK$15.60 while Kerry Properties gained HK$1.55 to HK$22.50. The Kerry share, which was offered at HK$17.50 and only 1.03 times subscribed in early August, was the best performing stock on Monday.
Some brokers continued to maintain a more cynical view of infrastructure plays.

"People are just buying laggards. It (Kerry) has been lagging behind the market for ages and the stock still provides a deep discount to NAV (net asset value)," said Antony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas.

Old China hand New World Infrastructure put on HK$0.10 to HK$19.60. The company announced earnings of HK$240.73 million for the six months to June 30, compared with HK$130.71 for the previous financial year.

Road King Infrastructure, which announced first half results showing net profit of HK$110.62 million, significantly better than the earnings forecast in its listing prospectus, rose HK$0.20 to HK$6.55.
Road King also was not well received when it came to the market in July, the local broker said.
